blocks.text: 1. Positional Encoding

blocks.alt: A token embedding adds to positional encoding to form the final input

blocks.text: The Decoder, the previous topic, completed the Transformer's own two-part architecture. Positional Encoding is the mechanism replacing the ordering information recurrence used to provide, explored throughout this topic.

It works by injecting genuinely explicit position information directly into each input representation, a genuinely essential, necessary companion to the architecture covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Missing Ordering Information

This connects back to no RNN or CNN involved, already covered in Transformer Architecture. Without recurrence, already covered there, the Transformer genuinely has no built-in sense of word order at all.
This topic genuinely delivers the direct, mathematical solution already previewed there, closing the exact gap already identified at that earlier point in this course.
3. Why Order Information Genuinely Gets Lost

blocks.alt: Self-attention has no inherent sense of order

blocks.text: This connects back to Self-Attention, already covered in its own topic. Self-Attention genuinely treats the input as an unordered set of positions, comparing every pair equally, already covered there.
Without any genuinely additional information, position 1 and position 10 would look genuinely identical, a genuinely real, structural consequence of Self-Attention's own permutation-invariant design.

blocks.text: 4. The Core Idea
Positional Encoding's genuinely core idea connects back to word embeddings, covered later in this course. Add a genuinely unique, position-specific vector directly to each input embedding.
This genuinely direct, simple fix, already covered in this section, restores exactly the position information already covered as lost in the previous section, without requiring any recurrence at all.
5. Sine And Cosine Functions

blocks.alt: A position produces a sine wave and a cosine wave

blocks.text: This connects back to Tanh, already covered in the Activation Functions module. The genuinely original formulation uses sine and cosine functions at genuinely different frequencies, a genuinely different mathematical family from Tanh.
This produces a genuinely unique, smoothly varying pattern for every single position, giving each position its own genuinely distinctive signature encoded directly into the input.
6. Why Sine And Cosine Specifically

blocks.alt: Sine and cosine give a unique, smooth pattern per position

blocks.text: A genuinely elegant mathematical property connects back to relative position, a genuinely important, real practical need. These specific functions genuinely let the model easily learn to attend based on genuinely relative position too.

This genuinely elegant property, already covered in this section, means the model can learn patterns like "the word two positions back" genuinely more easily than with a genuinely arbitrary encoding scheme.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This elegant mathematical property, already covered in this topic, is a genuinely important reason the original Transformer paper chose sine and cosine functions specifically, rather than some other arbitrary encoding scheme.

blocks.text: 7. Added, Not Concatenated

blocks.alt: Concatenated is compared against added directly

blocks.text: This connects back to concatenating the heads, already covered in Multi-Head Attention. Positional Encoding genuinely gets added directly to the input embedding, not genuinely concatenated alongside it.
This keeps the genuinely overall input dimension unchanged, a genuinely deliberate, efficient design choice, unlike the concatenation approach already covered for combining multiple attention heads.
8. A Preview Of Learned Positional Embeddings

blocks.alt: Fixed sine and cosine is compared against learned positional embeddings

blocks.text: A genuinely important, real alternative connects back to Embeddings, already covered generally throughout Feature Maps and elsewhere. Some genuinely modern architectures instead use genuinely learned positional embeddings.

This genuinely real alternative, already covered in this section, lets the network genuinely learn its own preferred position representation through training, rather than relying on the fixed sine and cosine pattern already covered earlier in this topic.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing Why Positional Encoding Is Genuinely Essential

blocks.alt: Using self-attention points toward needing positional encoding

blocks.text: This connects back to order genuinely mattering, already covered in Sequence Data. Positional Encoding, already covered in this topic, is genuinely required for the Transformer to respect that ordering at all.

Building any genuinely Attention-only architecture without recurrence or convolution is another genuine case where Positional Encoding, already covered, or a genuinely learned alternative, is genuinely non-negotiable.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates computing sine and cosine Positional Encoding vectors for several positions, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

def positional_encoding(position, hidden_size):
    # already covered as sine and cosine functions in this topic
    encoding = np.zeros(hidden_size)
    for i in range(0, hidden_size, 2):
        frequency = 1 / (10000 ** (i / hidden_size))
        encoding[i] = np.sin(position * frequency)
        if i + 1 < hidden_size:
            encoding[i + 1] = np.cos(position * frequency)
    return encoding

hidden_size = 6
for position in [0, 1, 5, 10]:
    encoding = positional_encoding(position, hidden_size)
    print(f"Position {position}: {np.round(encoding, 3)}")

print("\nNotice each position produces a genuinely unique, distinctive pattern, already covered in this topic")
